prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE premium, highly distinctive Continental Group homepage concept called "Le fil Continental". This is a graphic brand identity and scrollytelling direction, NOT a generic corporate landing template, NOT an art poster. Target dimensions: one long scrollable webpage 1440 x 2160, edge-to-edge website content, no browser, device, exterior frame, option numbers or designer annotations.
Reference roles: reference 1 is an OLD homepage used ONLY to understand the company's four business divisions and what visual language must be REPLACED. Do not copy the old split portrait hero, beige palette, serif typography, rounded masks or cards. Reference 2 is the OFFICIAL logo; preserve the recognizable green/gold Continental Group mark in a compact white header, not a redesigned wordmark.
The design's single signature is a visible fine gold binding thread that joins the page's chapters. Inspired by the honest structure of an exposed book binding, but translate that discipline into a MODERN FLAT WEBSITE: no literal book, wood covers, parchment, curved pages, thread photo background or skeuomorphic frame. The line is a functional progress/navigation axis. It is restrained, deliberate and visually continuous, not a network diagram, glowing cable, random squiggle or decoration across text.
Composition in order:
1. White compact header: original logo left; "Le Groupe", "Nos métiers", and a precise "Nous contacter" link at right. 80px high.
2. An exceptional full-width typographic opening, roughly 620px. Mostly WHITE with deep green type, asymmetric and exceptionally spacious. Main headline "Quatre métiers." on one line and "Un même fil." on the next, set like a confident contemporary brand identity in a broad elegant sans-serif resembling Hanken Grotesk, NOT condensed and NOT serif. Main heading is neither centered in a generic hero nor in a side panel next to a photo. Supporting text, readable and brief: "Commerce, énergie, logiciels et soin textile à Douala." Integrate a clever four-entry business directory into the opening: "Market", "Energy", "Software", "Pressing" with simple, clearly clickable typographic links, arranged as a single editorial list rather than cards. A thin gold thread starts near the logo and becomes a shared binding axis for this directory and the content below. One clear main action "Explorer nos métiers". A decisive wide photographic crop crosses the bottom of the opening: textures of an actual shop workbench with a laptop package and hands preparing an order, no posed faces. The headline, directory and photograph occupy different horizontal bands, NOT the standard half-copy half-photo layout.
3. The first scroll chapter, "Équiper le quotidien.", on a clean full-width white section. The persistent gold line at roughly the one-fifth-page axis marks "Market" active. Compose a LARGE broad documentary product-work image and a modest caption around this same axis, with the text "Téléphonie, informatique et équipement de la maison." and "Découvrir Market". Show the physical quality of materials, cardboard, electronics, detailed Black Cameroonian hands. Image has precise rectangular edges, no decorative rounded masks.
4. Next chapter begins with "Alimenter l'activité." on an exceptionally refined DEEP GREEN full-width surface with white text and one large close-up of clean installed energy equipment. The same gold line continues across the surface change and marks Energy. Image placement and scale differs from prior chapter. Names Software and Pressing remain legible in a compact persistent chapter index; their detailed sections may exist below the depicted crop. No four equal tiles.
5. Small closing invitation "Parlons de votre projet." with contact and understated brand signature.
Give the page a strong sustained axis, visual rhythm and generous negative space. A high-end printed identity translated into living web navigation. True white, rich forest green, one flat gold trace; no beige, no gradients, no glass, no shadows, no neon, no fake grain, no tiny uppercase labels above every title, no arbitrary numbering. No generic stock executive photos or smiling team collage. Maximum two type families, body text equivalent to 16px, thoughtful line lengths, all French spelled correctly. Sharp editorial photographs are art-direction proposals, not evidence of the actual company or its completed projects. No invented achievements, metrics, testimonials, dates, uniform logos or technical specifications. Show one coherent website design, no explanatory arrows or words about sticky/scroll implementation.
status: concept - photography generated for art direction, not documentary evidence
